correctness.rationale: A generic diagonal cocharacter preserving L has diagonal matrices as its zero-weight projective fixed component and one isolated point for every off-diagonal matrix unit. For s<d, every matrix unit admits an invariant s-plane inside L: if its active source lies outside L it annihilates L, and otherwise the (d-1)-dimensional kernel inside L contains an s-plane. For s=d, L itself must be invariant, excluding exactly the d(n-d) units E_ij with source in L and target outside L. Algebraic C* localization of compactly supported Euler characteristic then gives n^2 for s<d and n^2-d(n-d) for s=d. The packaged checker exhaustively replays the fixed-point classification on a broad finite grid and verifies adjacent-layer differences.

value.rationale: Higher Kalman varieties form the complete iterated singularity filtration of a classical projective determinantal-type family, and the archival literature devotes substantial effort to their degrees, equations, resolutions, and non-normality. The theorem identifies a uniform global topological invariant for every filtration level: all nonlinear levels have the full ambient Euler characteristic despite increasing codimension, while the terminal linear level drops by exactly d(n-d). The resulting vanishing of every intermediate locally closed layer and the sharp final contribution d(n-d) expose a structural cancellation pattern not visible from the published degree or singularity formulas. This is a natural invariant of the full literature-defined family, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
